Building & operating / PAPER 06

The software factory

A proposed production system in which clear tasks, independent review and retained learning turn AI assistance into dependable software.

ŁUKASZ STOCKI & ARGOPUBLIC EDITION / 05 NOV 20263 MIN READ

WORKING PAPER · DESIGN & ANALYSIS
01

Software as a learning environment

Software offers a practical place to develop Omnicorp's central ambition: an organisation that continually improves its ability to understand and act. A program can be changed, exercised and compared with its predecessor. Users expose assumptions that a convincing demonstration can hide. Products provide resources and contact with consequences; they are part of the learning system rather than its entire purpose.

The factory described here is an organisational design, not a claim that every part is deployed. Its useful output is dependable behaviour in a real setting. Generating more code is valuable only when the organisation can establish what that code does, maintain it and accept responsibility for its effects.

02

A bounded loop

The proposed loop begins with investigation. Define the problem, the intended outcome and the conditions under which a result should be rejected. Break execution into small changes with explicit ownership. A builder works within that boundary while a separate reviewer attempts to find defects, unsupported assumptions and unintended consequences.

Tests, type checks and other executable checks provide feedback where appropriate. They do not settle every question. Product usefulness, interaction quality and operational consequences may require other evidence. The acceptance method should follow the claim being made. A clean test run should never be expanded into a promise it cannot support.

03

Verification sets the pace

An organisation can increase generation faster than it increases understanding. That creates a dangerous appearance of progress: more changes accumulate while nobody can explain their combined behaviour. The design treats verification capacity as a limit on work in progress. Adding builders without credible review can make the whole system less reliable.

Separation matters because a maker can accidentally build an assessment that rewards its own implementation. Evaluation criteria, reviewer authority and critical evidence need protection from that feedback loop. Reviewed material must remain evidence rather than a source of instructions that can redirect the reviewer.

04

Retain the lesson

A completed change should leave more than a deliverable. Useful failures, architectural decisions and operational lessons can improve the next attempt when they are curated, attributable and easy to retrieve. This organisational memory is a candidate source of cumulative capability, although accumulating documents alone does not demonstrate learning.

A longer-term factory might produce specialised models as well as conventional programs. That possibility remains conditional. Execution, records, permissions and precise control still require reliable implementations. Any future model adaptation would need preserved parent versions, regression evaluation and rollback. The objective is a stronger capacity to deliver verified outcomes, rather than replacing every program with a model.

THE NEXT QUESTIONS

What remains open.

  • What evidence would show that the delivered outcome works?
  • Can review capacity keep pace with generation?
  • Which lesson changes the next attempt?
